# tmuxp example workspaces

The `.yaml` files in this directory are the workspace files in tmuxp's
[`examples/`](https://github.com/tmux-python/tmuxp/tree/153acdf6ff1268b14d3d03ed488f545a7123c8f1/examples)
directory at revision `153acdf6ff1268b14d3d03ed488f545a7123c8f1`, copied byte for byte. They are what
[tmuxp's configuration examples](https://tmuxp.git-pull.com/configuration/examples/)
page shows.

[`tmuxp-examples.test.ts`](../../tmuxp-examples.test.ts) runs
`tmux-workspace load -d` on each file against a private tmux server and
checks the windows and panes it builds. `plugin-system.yaml` is the one file
the CLI refuses, and the test asserts that refusal.

Do not edit these files. To follow tmuxp, copy the new versions over them and
change the revision above. A file that differs from tmuxp's is no longer an
example of tmuxp's.

## Expected structures

[`expected/`](expected) holds one JSON file for each workspace file the loader
reads on its own: the session, windows and panes that file means, with names,
indexes, layouts, focus, start directories, environment and the commands in the
order they are sent. They are written by hand from what tmuxp documents for each
example, not generated by running tmuxp, and no test needs tmuxp or Python.
[`tmuxp-structure.test.ts`](../../tmuxp-structure.test.ts) compares each with
the loaded model. `plugin-system.yaml` has no structure: its `plugins` run
through tmuxp's Python.

A file whose structure differs from tmuxp's is a bug to fix or a difference to
list here with its reason.

`${HOME}` stands for the home directory the test loads with, and
`${WORKSPACE_DIR}` for this directory. A value of `on` is the string tmux
receives, whichever way the YAML reader spells it.

The structures for nine files start from the ones libtmux-ruby wrote by hand
for the same catalog, at
[`test/fixtures/tmuxp/expected`](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/fdc8bac728380e78b8105198dd00868b83151e7e/test/fixtures/tmuxp/expected):
`2-pane-vertical`, `3-pane`, `4-pane`, `focus-window-and-panes`,
`main-pane-height`, `session-environment`, `shorthands`, `start-directory` and
`window-index`. Each differs from the original where this loader means
something else:

- `focus` is what the file declares. This loader keeps it as written and the
  builder leaves the last pane and the first window selected when none says
  otherwise; libtmux-ruby's loader set the first window and pane.
- `pane`, as a pane, is a blank pane, as `blank-panes.yaml` says. libtmux-ruby
  ran it as a command.
- An absolute `start_directory` is passed on as written, so `/var/` stays
  `/var/`; libtmux-ruby shortened it.
- Each pane also carries what this loader models and libtmux-ruby's does not:
  `shell`, `suppress_history` when it is off, and `enter`, `sleep_before` and
  `sleep_after` as the file declares them. A command with its own `enter` or
  `sleep_*` is an object; every other command is its text.

## Syntax support

[`syntax-support.json`](syntax-support.json) records, for each tmuxp key and
form, whether the loader supports it, supports it with a recorded difference, or
refuses it with a message. The same test reads each entry's probe through the
loader, so the record changes when the loader does.
